Yes. If by “small” you mean you talk directly to the person actually making the content—not an account manager who then briefs a junior team—I’d shortlist these Toronto options:

My top picks

1. Reet Media — probably the closest match
Reet Media

This is a genuinely boutique studio led by Gurleen, who is the founder, content creator, photographer and brand strategist. Reet says it deliberately limits the number of clients and gives them direct access rather than a template-driven agency experience. They do content production, photography/video, social strategy and content direction. 
Reet Media
+1

Reet Media

Why I'd start here: It sounds very close to what you're describing—one creative person who understands your brand and actually makes the work.

2. Scene Creative — excellent if you want one person handling your social
Scene Creative is a Toronto boutique social/content agency where the founder describes herself as personally handling strategy, creative direction and day-to-day social media management. 
Scene Creative Inc.

Scene Creative

Best for: Instagram/social content, ongoing management, and wanting a close creative relationship rather than a traditional agency structure.

This one is unusually explicit about the model: one dedicated strategist per client, with founder Roshan saying the person who writes your content is the person who picks up the phone. They combine strategy/copywriting with a production team for shooting and editing. 
RAMPD Vision

Best for: If you are the face of the business and want someone to develop your voice, write content and turn your expertise into social/video.

4. KO 360 — great if video/storytelling is the priority

It's founder-led by two former BBC journalists, Aishwarya and Sairam. They personally work on interviews, scripting, creative direction, production and strategy rather than treating content as generic social posts. 
KO 360

Best for: Thought leadership, talking-head video, personal branding and storytelling.

If I were choosing for you

I'd contact Reet Media first, then Scene Creative.

They seem most aligned with the specific thing you're asking for: “I want to know and work directly with the creative person, not be passed around an agency.”

If you tell me what kind of business you have + roughly what you want to spend per month (e.g. $1–2k, $2–4k, $5k+), I can narrow this down to 3 Toronto studios that are specifically a fit for your type of content and budget.
